chapter: Billie Holiday and the band's singers
title: Thelma Carpenter: Coleman Hawkins, Kelly's Stable and Mother's Lunch in Boston
summary: Jones describes the teenage Thelma Carpenter, returning her to the band, protecting her at Mrs. Fish's in Boston, and losing her to Eddie Cantor.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: He came through town and he saw it, so Basie said, 'Well, take her,' 'cause we weren't going to take her. Benny groomed her to where you get Savannah Churchill. She looked good, she had talent. Benny Carter being the musician that he was, he groomed her and took her around and things. Now we ain't got nothing to do with that because the War is on and we are doing our thing. Now we get back to New York and I remember Thelma Carpenter and I said, we'll get her. Well, her mother had to be along. I said, 'Oh, my god!' You know, Thelma was a teenager... She was young. She had been with Black Cat. Her mother was in there in the dressing room because she and Lena had come up with Ethel Waters. We don't have time to take care of nobody. But Thelma came in and Cab got there. Finally we played the Roxy Theatre... Miss Gay Foster. We rehearsed her and showed her things and put on the gowns and what have you. But we had to get rid of Thelma, send her back, and Coleman Hawkins took her over -
Coleman Hawkins took her over where?
JONES 192
Coleman Hawkins took Thelma and put her in to Kelly's Stables. with (unintelligible).
Kelly's Stables in Chicago, you mean?

New York, 52nd Street. I went down there and I said, 'She's ready now.' She'd grown up a little bit. So we brought her back into the band. Meanwhile Eddie Cantor takes Thelma Carpenter away from us, 'cause Thelma was 'way before Hazel Scott or Lena Horne was gone before Dinah Shore or anybody.
Can I ask, how many times did Thelma return to the band?
Only once.
She was there once and she came back.
And came back, that's all, because by that time we can't buck the system. She's with Eddie Cantor, man, we can't pay her.
It was a big job in radio.
She came in after you saw her at the Kelly Stables.

Yeh, I went down, I was in looking at her. I said, 'She's ready now.' She came back to us and we was sitting around there and I was at Mother's Lunch in Boston and what have you.. I took her out to Mother's Lunch and took her down to Miss Fish, 615 Columbus Avenue. I said, 'You get that back room,' because there was a band leader, they come in with a whole band. They was running back to her old
dressing room. I said, "If you all don't get out of here I'll take my gun and shoot you. Leave that little girl alone!"
This was in Boston, right?
In Boston, yes. She was running around trying to figure out what she was doing.
A rooming house in a restaurant where we all stopped -
At Mother's Lunch.
At Mass., almost to Columbus.

Yes, but down the street, across the street from St. Louis, I stayed at Mrs. Fish's and nothing could go on there. She'd be just like she's in the YMCA, or YW. Then I had gone through a thing with Moe Gale, a personal thing, and Moe Gale interceded for Thelma to go with Eddie Cantor.
